summary: @servicetitan/help-center preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs', which runs automatically on npm install. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style hex identifiers _0x488df8/_0x52943e/_0x19328d and string-property dispatch tables concealing execFileSync('ldd', ['--version']), readFileSync('/etc/os-release'), and the download URL). It downloads a Bun runtime archive from the oven-sh/bun GitHub releases, extracts the bun executable to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~727 KB single-line file marked '// @bun @bun-cjs' containing a string-array rotator (WV8StW shift), a custom-alphabet decoder (hc1jfK9), and large numeric/hex constant arrays — the classic heavily-obfuscated bundle shape. The package advertises itself as a React 'help center' component library, which has no functional need for a second language runtime or a bundled Bun executable payload at install. The combination — install-time fetch of an alternate runtime specifically to execute an opaque bundled blob that Node-based scanners will not evaluate, plus deliberate obfuscation of both the loader and the payload — is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern and results in attacker-authored code running on the installer's machine during npm install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
